thread:
acme-app: Hey team — over the last hour our app started seeing intermittent 429s and long tail latency even though we have a Dedicated reserved pool (acct: acme-42). Seems to coincide with a nightly job spike. Can you help triage?

maya-support: Sorry about that — can you paste the exact timestamps and the request IDs from the error responses? Also which model and region are you hitting (e.g., redwood/gptq-13b-us-west)?

acme-app: Timestamps: 2026-03-16T02:13:10Z to 02:18:40Z. Example response headers: `x-rw-rate-limit: 1200/1200`, `x-rw-reserved-pool: acme-42`, `x-rw-fallback: hosted`. Body error: `429: capacity_exceeded`. We were calling streaming generation with concurrency 12 and max_tokens 1024. Model: rw/gptq-13b-8bit-us-west.

ravi-oncall: Thanks — two immediate suspects: (1) reserved pool ran out and requests fell back to hosted (billing note), (2) streaming + high concurrency causing token-burst behavior and hitting per-shard caps. Can you share a trimmed repro script?

acme-app: here's a small repro we ran:```bash
for i in {1..12}; do
  curl -s -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"rw/gptq-13b-8bit-us-west","input":"summarize: ...","max_tokens":1024,"stream":true}' \
    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
done
wait
```

maya-support: That helps. The headers you pasted show `x-rw-reserved-pool` present but the `x-rw-fallback: hosted` means some backend requests couldn't be served by the reserved pool and we routed to hosted to keep requests alive. That explains the capacity_exceeded 429 responses and the billing fallback.

jules-infra: Quick infra note: reserved pools allocate token bandwidth across nodes; burst capacity exists but there's a per-instance throughput cap (qps/tokens/s) and a refill algorithm (token-bucket). Streaming large max_tokens with many concurrent streams can deplete the bucket faster than intended.

acme-app: Could you explain why we saw fallbacks instead of queueing? Our SLA expects dedicated to absorb short spikes.

ravi-oncall: Policy: we prefer graceful fallback to hosted when reserved pool cannot maintain latency SLOs, rather than queueing and increasing user p99. That behavior is configurable with the customer's rollout policy (canary vs strict). Looks like your account is set to `prefer_fallback: true` which causes immediate fallback on shortfall.

ben-billing: FYI — fallback to hosted will be billed at hosted rates. I can run a delta for the hour if you want. @acme-app do you want us to flag these fallback events so we can credit unexpected charges?

acme-app: Yes please, credit request and we want a mitigation plan. Also we saw a handful of 401s interleaved during rotation windows — unrelated?

maya-support: 401s could be token rotation from your side or short-lived keys expired. Any details?

acme-app: We rotate keys every 5m via our internal vault. The 401s line up with rotations at 02:15:30Z. But most 429s are earlier at 02:14:50Z.

jules-infra: Two-prong suggestion: (A) short term: lower `max_tokens` for streaming or reduce concurrency to smooth token drain; (B) medium term: request an increase to your reserved pool burst parameter and change `prefer_fallback` to `queue_during_spike` for 30s windows (requires support config change). Also we can enable per-route burst cushions in the console.

ravi-oncall: Repro notes for eng — logs show per-shard token bucket drained to 0 at 02:14:52Z and then we started returning 429s and routing 40% of traffic to hosted until refill. I'll attach the shard-level CSV in support ticket.

acme-app: Can you provide the exact config keys we should change? Console steps are fine.

maya-support: We can do this via the Console -> Reserved Pools -> acme-42 -> Edit policy: set "burst_headroom_tokens" to 150000 and "fallback_policy" to "queue_for_20s_then_fallback". On API it looks like:```json
{"pool_id":"acme-42","burst_headroom_tokens":150000,"fallback_policy":"queue_for_20s_then_fallback"}
```

ben-billing: I've flagged the hour for review — please confirm you want a one-time courtesy credit for post-fallback usage.

acme-app: Yes, please. We'll also throttle the nightly job. Could you confirm if enabling queueing risks p99 latency violations?

jules-infra: Queueing trades immediate latency for eventual completion; our default queue timeout is 25s. If your consumer can't tolerate >200ms p99, fallback is still the safer option. For batch jobs that can wait, queueing is fine.

ravi-oncall: Action items: (1) Support — submit config change to ops to increase burst_headroom and switch policy (maya), (2) Infra — evaluate per-shard cap increase and confirm no cross-customer impact (jules), (3) Billing — review charges and apply credit if approved (ben), (4) Acme — throttle nightly job and rotate keys with slight overlap to avoid 401s during high concurrency (acme-app).

acme-app: Thanks all — please paste ticket/PR numbers when done. :pray:

deploy-bot: [deploy] reserved-pool-config update requested by maya-support — job queued (#56784).

maya-support: Filed ticket SUP-2026-411. I'll post back when ops confirms the change and when Ben confirms billing.

acme-app: Received — will throttle job tonight and rerun the repro in the morning. Appreciate the quick triage. :thumbsup:
